data.narrative:
Firefly Aerospace is a public-stage space and aerospace company currently valued at approximately $2.9 billion. The comparable universe consists of five publicly traded space and aerospace peers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and eight private frontier-tech companies operating in adjacent segments, including Rocket Lab, Planet Labs, and Astroscale.

The peer-median method is the primary applicable valuation approach. Based on three same-sector, same-stage comparables—Rocket Lab ($40.0B), Planet Labs ($7.6B), and Astroscale ($840M)—the median peer valuation is $7.6 billion. This reflects substantial dispersion in the comp set, with a range spanning from $840 million to $40.0 billion. A public-comp anchoring methodology using the sector's 27.4x price-to-sales median could not be applied due to the absence of target revenue data, which is typical for private or recently public frontier-tech operators.

The triangulated analysis, constrained by the applicability of a single method, supports a valuation range of $6.4 billion (low) to $8.7 billion (high), with a median of $7.6 billion. This implies the current $2.9 billion valuation sits notably below peer medians, though the wide dispersion in comparables—spanning nearly two orders of magnitude—introduces material uncertainty. Key unknowns include revenue trajectory, capital efficiency relative to peers, and contract book visibility, all of which would refine the valuation band.
